title: Methods and legend for predicted osteoarthritis effector genes
bodyHtml:
These manually curated effector gene predictions were generated by the Genetics of Osteoarthritis Consortium and were published by Boer, Hatzikotoulas, Southam, et al., 2021.

Additional evidence supporting the predictions is available in Table S12 of the publication.

 

Main column headers (summarized predictions)

Gene: the predicted osteoarthritis effector gene. Gene names are linked to the corresponding Gene page in the Musculoskeletal Knowledge Portal.

Score: cumulative score for each gene based on the supporting fine-mapping and functional analysis. Genes are assigned a score from 1 to 6, with 6 representing the strongest evidence.

Druggable Genome Tier: a classification of potentially druggable gene products as defined by Finan et al., 2017. Tier 1 includes efficacy targets of approved small molecules and biotherapeutic drugs, and clinical-phase drug candidates. Tier 2 includes targets with known bioactive drug-like small molecule binding partners and gene products with ≥50% identity (over ≥75% of the sequence) with approved drug targets. Tier 3 includes genes encoding secreted or extracellular proteins, proteins with more distant similarity to approved drug targets, and members of key druggable gene families not already included in Tiers 1 or 2, such as GPCRs, nuclear hormone receptors, ion channels, kinases, and phosphodiesterases. This tier was further subdivided to prioritize those genes that were in proximity (±50 kbp) to a GWAS SNP from the GWAS catalog and had an extracellular location (Tier 3A). The remainder of the genes was assigned to Tier 3B.

Signal: a number identifying the osteoarthritis genetic association signal in this study.

Lead OA SNV: rsID of the lead variant at the locus.

EA: effect allele.

EAF: effect allele frequency.

New/Known signal: N indicates that a signal was newly identified in this study; K indicates that it was previously known. Using an approximate conditional and joint multiple-SNP analysis, as implemented by COJO in GCTA (Yang et al., 2012; Yang et al., 2011), we investigated the statistical independence between index signals per osteoarthritis phenotype and previously reported osteoarthritis variants within a 1-Mb region. The index variant was classified as a new association if it had a conditional p ≤ 1x10−7 or the P value difference between conditional and unconditional analysis increased by more than two orders of magnitude. Index variants were classified as known if they have previously been reported or the association signal disappeared after conditioning on the variant of a previously reported locus.

Biological classification: biological processes related to osteoarthritis in which the gene product may be involved, as suggested by published evidence. See Table S12 of the publication for references.

Nested table headers (supporting evidence)

Genetic evidence types

Coding variant and fine map: the gene in which the lead variant has moderate to high severity consequences, as predicted by haploR, OR the gene in which a moderate to high severity variant is in high LD (r2 ≥ 0.8) with the lead SNV and is present in the 95% credible set. Consequences classified as moderate to high severity by haploR are: transcript_ablation, splice_acceptor, splice_donor, stop_gained, frameshift, stop_lost, start_lost, transcript_amplification, inframe_insertion, inframe_deletion, missense, and protein_altering.

Fine mapped gene: all variants in the 95% credible set reside within the transcript of this gene.

Regulatory evidence types

eQTL localization (GTEx/OA tissue): the gene was colocalized in at least 1 GTEx tissue with the number of GTEx tissues in parentheses followed by the number of these tissues that were also enriched in tissue enrichment analysis, which is suggestive of a role in osteoarthritis pathology.

Cartilage expression: the gene was differentially expressed in high-grade compared to low-grade osteoarthritic cartilage or bone.  (+) indicates increased expression in degraded cartilage or bone and (-) indicates decreased expression in degraded cartilage or bone.

Cartilage abundance: the gene codes for a protein that was differentially expressed in high-grade compared to low-grade osteoarthritic cartilage.  (+) indicates increased protein abundance in degraded cartilage and (-) indicates decreased protein abundance in degraded cartilage.

Bone expression: the gene was differentially expressed in subchondral bone.

Blood pQTL MR + coloc: the gene was identified as being on the causal path in the Mendelian Randomization and was also colocalized.

Phenotypic evidence types:

Mouse musculoskeletal phenotype: a musculoskeletal (skeleton, limb/digit/tail, and muscle) phenotype included in the MGI mouse phenotype ontology is observed in a knockout of the mouse homolog, as cataloged by Butterfield et al., 2021 or in the MGI Mouse Genome Informatics database.

Human musculoskeletal phenotype: gene linked to a musculoskeletal phenotype according to the nosology and classification of genetic skeletal disorders (Mortier et al., 2019).

Mouse neuronal phenotype: a neuronal phenotype ("nervous system phenotype" included in the MGI mouse phenotype ontology) is observed in a knockout of the mouse homolog, as cataloged by Butterfield et al., 2021 or in the MGI Mouse Genome Informatics database.

Human pain disorder: the gene is linked to a pain or neuropathy disorder in the Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) database.

Human pain gene: the gene is linked to pain in the Human Pain Genetics Database (HPGD).
